title: parseInt on a number input silently truncates exponent input: typing 1e2 saves 1 minute
evidence: index.html:17 is type=number min=1 max=600, which accepts "1e2" as a valid value (100). Its .value string is "1e2". parseInt("1e2", 10) returns 1, which passes the `minutes > 0` check at app.js:22 and is stored and added to the total.
failing_case: Type 1e2 in Minutes and submit. The browser accepts it. The recipe is saved as 1 minute and the status reports a total that is 99 minutes short.
remediation: Read `valueAsNumber` (or Number(value)) and require Number.isInteger(minutes) with 1 <= minutes <= 600. Do not parse a numeric input with parseInt.

title: Delete ignores the save result and announces "Deleted" even when nothing was persisted
evidence: saveRecipes returns false on a storage error (store.js:17-19). The add handler checks that result (app.js:24-25); the delete handler discards it and always sets 'Deleted ...' (app.js:36). Driven in Chromium: setItem forced to throw, Delete clicked, status read 'Deleted “X”.' while localStorage still held the recipe.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. The user deletes a recipe and is told 'Deleted “X”.' The list re-renders without it. After a reload the recipe is back, because nothing was written.
remediation: Check the boolean from saveRecipes in the delete handler. On failure keep the old list (or say plainly that the change lasts only until the tab closes), as the add path already does.

quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or partly invalid stored data loads as an empty list with no message, and the next save permanently overwrites it; the comment claims app.js tells the user, it does not
evidence: No code in app.js reads a load failure; loadRecipes returns [] for both a blocked store and bad JSON (store.js:9), and the filter at store.js:7 drops entries silently. Driven: localStorage 'recipes' set to '{bad json', page reloaded: empty-state shown, status empty. Adding one recipe then replaced the raw value with a one-item list.
failing_case: A stored value fails JSON.parse (truncated write, manual edit, another version). The user sees 'No recipes yet. Add your first one above.' and adds a recipe. The old data, which might have been recoverable, is overwritten without notice. Same for any entry dropped by the name filter.
remediation: Return a result object ({list, error}) from loadRecipes. When parsing fails, copy the raw string to a backup key before any write, show a status message in app.js, and do not save over the corrupt value until the user chooses to.

title: Every save overwrites the whole stored list from a copy read once at page load, so a second tab silently destroys the first tab's recipes
evidence: app.js:3 reads recipes once; each add or delete writes the entire in-memory array (store.js:15) with no re-read, no 'storage' event listener and no version. Driven: two pages of one browser context, tab A added 'fromA', tab C (loaded before that) added 'fromC'. localStorage then held only fromC.
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. Add a recipe in tab 1. Add a different recipe in tab 2. Tab 1's recipe is gone from storage and from every later load. The user is told 'Saved' both times.
remediation: Re-read the stored list immediately before each write and merge by id (or apply add/delete as operations on the freshly read list). Listen to the 'storage' event to refresh the view.

title: Deleting a recipe destroys the focused Delete button and focus falls to the body
evidence: The click handler rebuilds listEl.innerHTML (app.js:10) after the confirm. Driven: focused a Delete button, pressed Enter, accepted the confirm; document.activeElement was BODY. Status is announced via role=status (index.html:20), but the keyboard position is lost. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A).
failing_case: A keyboard or switch user deletes the first of ten recipes. Focus resets to the top of the document and they must Tab through the form again to reach the next Delete button.
remediation: After render, move focus to the next (or previous) item's Delete button, or to the 'Your recipes' heading made focusable with tabindex=-1 when the list is empty.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Load only checks name; records with no id or a non-numeric minutes pass through and break Delete and the total
evidence: Driven with stored [{name:'Old',minutes:'20'},{name:'B',minutes:'x'}]: list shows 'B NaN min'; clicking Delete throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')' (recipes.find at app.js:32 finds no id, r is undefined at app.js:33; the comment at app.js:14 says that cannot happen) and the item stays; after adding a recipe the status read 'Total cooking time: 020x5 minutes.' (string concatenation in store.js:23).
failing_case: Saved data from an older shape (no id, minutes as a string) or edited by hand. The record can never be deleted (the click handler throws before the confirm), and the total shown after the next add is garbage.
remediation: Normalise at the load boundary: assign a fresh id when missing, coerce minutes with Number and drop or flag records where it is not a finite positive number. Add a versioned saved shape.
